empirical_analysis.reasoning: Voiceover path normalizes to -16 LUFS (voiceover.py VOICE_CLARITY_TARGET_I_LUFS, verified in source). Required cut = voice_lufs + 10*log10(0.3) - music_lufs = voice_lufs - 10.46 - music_lufs. Realistic loud commercial music (-6..-14 LUFS) against -16..-23 LUFS voiceovers requires at most -29.5 dB of cut (voice -23 / music -6). No real signal measures far above +3 LUFS integrated (full-scale square wave is the physical ceiling), so the worst physically possible cut is ~-36.5 dB. New floor -60 dB leaves >23 dB of headroom beyond that while still clamping absurd demands from corrupt/misparsed readings (e.g. a reading tens of dB above digital full scale). The old -40 dB floor sat only ~3.5 dB below the physical ceiling — one unusual measurement away from under-correcting. MAX kept at +24 dB, independently justified: boosting a quiet file amplifies its noise floor by the same amount, so the boost side is deliberately conservative; +24 dB covers music down to ~-50 LUFS under -16 LUFS vocals. NOTE: the empirical matrix shows no REALISTIC loud-music combination ever reached the old -40 floor — any clamping it applied was by definition to non-physical readings — so if the operator's symptom persists after this fix, the next suspect is the measurement path itself (what loudnorm returns for the specific failing upload), not the clamp.
